heading: Whether a neuron looks polysemantic depends on activation range and scoring method
definition: whether a neuron counts as polysemantic depends on which part of its activation range is examined and how explanations are scored.
summary: Several independent groups find that polysemanticity judgments shift with the activation range examined and with the scoring method, in language models up to Llama-3.1-8B and in vision CNNs, and no study contradicts this. Still, much of the activation-range evidence rests on single neurons, and some neurons stay polysemantic at every threshold tested.

suggested_status.by_scale: <1B: R2 from groups other than the original's: GPT-2 117M (arXiv:2604.00443), Whisper tiny (lw:thePw6qdyabD8XR4y), BERT-base (arXiv:2104.07143), Pythia 70M feature-dataset dependence (arXiv:2503.23298). The Pythia 70M activation-range evidence of arXiv:2305.01610 (r1, r2) is R1 only, because that study shares an author with the original. 1-10B: R2 from Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (arXiv:2502.16994), Llama-3.2-3B (arXiv:2502.06809; two neurons, qualitative) and GPT-2 XL (arXiv:2309.10312). Pythia 1B/6.9B (arXiv:2305.01610) is R1 (shared author). Gemma 3 4B (arXiv:2610.24521) shares no author with the original, but its authors are Anthropic-affiliated, the original's lab: R1 or R2 is Iris's call. R0 at 10-100B: counts versions.V7.studies_by_size.10-100B is 1; the pack's 12B subject is Pythia-12B in arXiv:2402.01702, one neuron read qualitatively. Untested above 100B (studies_by_size has no >100B key). Vision CNNs of unstated size: R2, from several groups (arXiv:1711.05611, arXiv:2007.01062, arXiv:2404.06453, arXiv:2508.16950). Toy: R0 (arXiv:2410.06232, linear RNN, conditioning choice only).
suggested_status.reason: No study challenges V7 (counts: versions.V7.verdicts.challenges.studies is 0). limits_scope verdicts (counts: versions.V7.studies_with_limits_scope is 6) confine where the dependence holds. First, AlexNet fc8 output units, where only human activation-maximisation interpretation was compared with class measures (arXiv:2007.01062 R16). Second, neurons that stay polysemantic at every threshold reported (arXiv:2304.09707 r4). Third, a small per-neuron effect between the most- and least-activated of each GPT2-XL layer-1 neuron's 100 core tokens (arXiv:2505.07831 R1). Its authors expect larger differences outside the core set, and the same study's averaged neuron supports V7 (R2-R4). Groups other than the original's show activation-range dependence on Pythia-12B (arXiv:2402.01702, one neuron) and Llama-3.2-3B (arXiv:2502.06809, two neurons, qualitative). They also show it in a vision CNN, where Network Dissection's τ is the activation top-quantile cutoff (arXiv:1711.05611 r9, r10). They show scoring dependence on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (arXiv:2502.16994), GPT-2 XL (arXiv:2309.10312) and vision CNNs (arXiv:1711.05611; arXiv:2007.01062, which measures class selectivity rather than polysemanticity). Not counted as independent: arXiv:2305.01610. The studies index marks it SAME GROUP, and its author list is marked as sharing authors with an original. Its V7 pack header does not carry this flag. Its Pythia activation-range evidence (r1-r4) and scoring evidence (r8-r10) are therefore R1. No other study the studies index marks SAME GROUP has a V7 verdict, so arXiv:2305.01610 is the study behind counts: versions.V7.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original is 1. arXiv:2610.24521 (Gemma 3 4B, R1, R2) shares no author with the original, but its authors are Anthropic-affiliated, the original's lab. The original's own evidence is one stricter rater and one unblinded neuron (TITLE:Softmax Linear Units R5, R7). Much of the activation-range evidence is single neurons or figure only (counts: versions.V7.rows_by_evidence_form.figure_only is 18). The counts code no causal operation for V7 (counts: versions.V7.coverage_by_operation has only evaluation, measurement and probing), but pack lines for arXiv:2405.06855 and arXiv:2309.10312 report causal operations that have no rows. arXiv:2405.06855 (ICML, code, controls): its header says it measures neuron impact through ablation and activation-ranked input fractions. Its method-sensitivity line says the measured share of causal impact depends strongly on the fraction of highest-activating inputs examined and varies by ResNet-50 layer. Its V7 verdict cites only R31, and its problems line calls the Top Impact results aggregates. arXiv:2309.10312: its header says it evaluates natural-language explanations against generated observational datasets and 'causal interch…' (the header is cut off there). Its method-sensitivity line says results differ between observational and intervention evaluations, and intervention effects increase when larger percentages of neurons are selected. The line is cut off at 'These intervention results do not directl…'. The studies index marks neither study SAME GROUP.
suggested_status.open_questions: (1) A population-level, numeric count of neurons that switch classification between top and quantile or lower ranges, across several LM families, from a group other than the original's. (2) A study in a large LM showing classifications stable across ranges and scorers, which would turn the limits into a challenge. (3) Row-level causal tests of which measurement's classification tracks a neuron's function. The pack has only method and header lines on this: ablation impact share by fraction of top inputs (arXiv:2405.06855), and observational vs intervention evaluations differing (arXiv:2309.10312). (4) Any test above 100B, and a test at 10-100B beyond one Pythia-12B neuron. (5) Whether arXiv:2610.24521 counts as independent. It shares no author by name, but its authors are at Anthropic, the original's lab. Iris rules on this.

source.title: Softmax Linear Units
source.authors: Nelson Elhage; Tristan Hume; Catherine Olsson; Neel Nanda; Tom Henighan; Scott Johnston; Sheer El Showk; Nicholas Joseph; Nova DasSarma; Ben Mann; Danny Hernandez; Amanda Askell; Kamal Ndousse; Andy Jones; Dawn Drain; Anna Chen; Yuntao Bai; Deep Ganguli; Liane Lovitt; Zac Hatfield-Dodds; Jackson Kernion; Tom Conerly; Shauna Kravec; Stanislav Fort; Saurav Kadavath; Josh Jacobson; Eli Tran-Johnson; Jared Kaplan; Jack Clark; Tom Brown; Sam McCandlish; Dario Amodei; Christopher Olah

original_result.setup: Author raters judged whether MLP neurons' top dataset examples were interpretable, comparing baseline and SoLU transformers.
original_result.result: One stricter annotator marked about 20% of baseline neurons and about 60% of SoLU neurons interpretable, against about 40% and 60% from the other two annotators. For one SoLU neuron, examples with low activation after LayerNorm were much more often unrelated to the neuron's proposed explanation, shown only in a figure and not blinded.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: The apparent meaning of BERT [CLS] units changed with the evaluation dataset used.
One neuron looked monosemantic or polysemantic (one or two concepts) depending on the clustering threshold.
A Pythia neuron looked narrow on top examples but polysemantic on a wider corpus.
Share of polysemantic audio neurons varied with τ and top-K; cross-model trends persisted.
CLIP and attribution scoring disagreed on which ResNet-50 neurons are polysemantic.
Polysemanticity rankings shifted with the number of top image patches used and the CLIP text head.
Polysemanticity's trend across layers reversed when patches were chosen by attribution relevance rather than activation.
Gemma-2-2B units active for several concepts sometimes had separable activation distributions.
A GPT-2 XL neuron earlier labelled possibly monosemantic showed several concepts when PRISM sampled more widely.
Pythia 70M FKR ranged from 5.2% to 67% depending only on the feature dataset.
For an averaged GPT2-XL neuron, the top-activating tokens were the most alike, making it look homogeneous.
Llama-3.2-3B neurons matched one class near their mean activation, drifting to other classes at range edges.
Gemma 3 4B neurons matched transcoder features' interpretability at peak activations but degraded across activation quantiles.
Discounting overlap from shared word forms reclassified 6.5–10.4% of GPT-2 neurons flagged as polysemantic.
Raw DINOv2 dimensions scored higher than SAE features on one monosemanticity metric, lower on another.
Two Whisper tiny neurons seemed single-phoneme at max activation, polysemantic at lower ranges.
AlexNet conv5 unit labels moved from painting or horse to brown as the activation cutoff loosened.
Hidden CNN units looked like object detectors on some selectivity measures but not others.
GPT-2 XL neurons with high GPT-4 explanation scores showed many off-explanation activations.
Pythia-12B neuron L10.N5 read monosemantic above activation 5, polysemantic below.
Interpretability scores fell for query images at mid-range activations and shifted with the image-similarity metric.
A ResNet-50 neuron's dog-related role appeared only at lower activations.
Linear RNN neurons looked mixed only when the analysis did not condition on a correlated source.
SAE rankings against CRATE flipped between OpenAI and Anthropic interpretability metrics.
A Llama-3.1-8B neuron's explanation scored well in simulation, but its strong activations were not concept-specific.
Judged monosemanticity fell as the VLM judge saw more top-activating images.
Model interpretability ordering flipped between raw purity and shuffle-corrected specificity.
Pythia-70M neuron directions beat random ones on top-and-random-example scoring, but explanations missed variation within text fragments.
Rater strictness and activation range changed how interpretable MLP neurons appeared.
One neuron stayed polysemantic at every clustering threshold reported, though its number of concept clusters changed.
In single GPT2-XL neurons, top and bottom tokens differed little; only 22.8% of neurons differed significantly.
Reading by activation range left some GPT-2 neurons polysemantic; one neuron's per-class activation distributions fully overlapped.
For AlexNet output units, human interpretation and class-selectivity measures agreed about 95%.
Neurons stayed less interpretable than activation-space directions under every image-similarity metric and query difficulty tested.
Restricting Pythia-70M MLP neurons to higher activations barely changed their interpretability scores.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

Population-level range results in arXiv:2610.24521 (R1, R2) and arXiv:2606.03990 (R16, R17) are figure only. counts: versions.V7.rows_by_evidence_form.figure_only is 18.

counts: versions.V7.studies_by_size has no >100B key; 10-100B is 1.

untested.basis: counts: versions.V7.studies_by_family lists only 'other or not stated', Pythia, GPT-2, Llama and Gemma.

untested.what: Whether the judge or explainer model changes which individual neurons are classified polysemantic.
untested.basis: Untested-parts lines: arXiv:2611.03655 (only one judge), arXiv:2606.03990 (no comparison of judges). lw:ursraZGcpfMjCXtnn uses one explainer (GPT-4) and one simulator (GPT-3.5). It compares three score splits (top-and-random, top-only, random-only) but classifies no individual neuron as polysemantic. The pack records explainer or simulator substitutions only for aggregate scores (arXiv:2410.16443 not-in-rows, Tables 6-7; arXiv:2609.35020 method-sensitivity line).

untested.what: Re-running the original's own protocol (rating of top pre-LayerNorm examples, 80% threshold, inspection time) with lower or post-LayerNorm activation ranges, or with automated scoring, on SoLU or comparable models.
untested.basis: Untested-parts line of TITLE:Softmax Linear Units (no systematic comparison of scoring rules, the 80% threshold, inspection time or automated explanations; one neuron for the activation-range check). No other study in the pack uses SoLU models.

wording_issues.phrase: which part of its activation range is examined and how explanations are scored
wording_issues.issue: Measurement choices other than these two also change the outcome. Evaluation dataset: BERT-base units average 2.5 distinct patterns across datasets (arXiv:2104.07143 R2). Feature dataset: Pythia 70M FKR is 5.2%, 21.8% or 67% depending on the dataset (arXiv:2503.23298 R25-R27). Conditioning variables: linear-RNN neurons go from single-source to mixed when one object is omitted (arXiv:2410.06232 R8, R9). Word-form confounds: ≈57% of flagged GPT-2 pairs share a word form (arXiv:2604.00443 r27). Clustering thresholds, embedding models and selectivity statistics (studies in 'also') are further choices, and several of them are not scored explanations.

wording_issues.phrase: whether a neuron counts as polysemantic
wording_issues.issue: Several results show that aggregate scores, or rankings of models and bases, depend on the metric, not that per-neuron classification does. Examples: GPT2-SAE vs CRATE (arXiv:2410.16443 r32-r37); MoE, dense and MoWE (arXiv:2611.03655 r1-r3, r11-r13); arXiv:2609.35020, whose untested line says it does not classify individual neurons. Per-neuron flips with activation range rest on single hand-picked neurons read qualitatively, e.g. Pythia-12B L10.N5 (arXiv:2402.01702 R1, R2).

The dependence does not show up in every setting tested. AlexNet fc8 output units: the only comparison run at fc8 (human reading of activation-maximisation images vs class measures) agrees. Among the 59.3% (±1.6) of units with at least 80% 'yes' responses, humans matched the most-active image's class 95.4% (±0.6) and the CCMAS class 94.6% (±0.7) (arXiv:2007.01062 R13, R16). fc8 got no signal-detection measures, and the study's main result is that measures disagree in hidden layers. Inception V3 Mixed 7b neuron 35 stays polysemantic at every dmax reported (arXiv:2304.09707 r4). Pythia-70M MLP layer 1, neuron basis and random directions: adding bias+ReLU gave no noticeable improvement in top-and-random auto-interp scores, while random-only scores 'perhaps rise slightly' (lw:ursraZGcpfMjCXtnn r4). These are mean scores, figure only, and the authors call them preliminary. GPT2-XL layer 1, 614 neurons: the 10 most-activated and 10 least-activated of each neuron's 100 core tokens differ by mean δ = .0274 (Cliff's delta .2407; 22.8% locally significant) (arXiv:2505.07831 R1). That compares ranges within the top 100 only. The authors expect larger differences for tokens outside the core set.

A wider range or a coarser score can turn an apparent mixture into one broader concept instead of revealing more concepts. AlexNet conv5 units selective for painting or horse at tight τ are labelled brown at loose τ (arXiv:1711.05611 r10). Inception V3 neuron 1 becomes one cluster above dmax 17 (arXiv:2304.09707 r6). For ResNet-50 #271, CLIP splits dogs from windmills while attributions show one triangular-shape semantic (arXiv:2404.06453 r24). A Pythia 6.9B neuron's low precision reflects a coarser related feature (arXiv:2305.01610 r10). The statement does not name concept granularity as a measurement choice.

wording_issues.phrase: which part of its activation range is examined
wording_issues.issue: The results run one way: top activations look monosemantic, while lower or quantile-sampled ranges look mixed (arXiv:2402.01702 R1, R2; arXiv:2610.24521 R1, R2). 'Range' is operationalised in different ways: an activation cutoff (above vs up to 5, arXiv:2402.01702), quantile sampling (arXiv:2610.24521), the number of top images k (arXiv:2606.03990 R16, R17) or the number of top patches K (arXiv:2508.16950 r18).

method_sensitivity.factor: Activation range or sampling of examples
method_sensitivity.what: Gemma 3 4B L22 sort evals: neurons score about as well as transcoder features with top sampling but degrade under quantile sampling (R1, R2; figure only). Pythia-12B L10.N5 reads monosemantic above activation 5 and polysemantic up to 5 (R1, R2). The VLM-judged monosemanticity rate falls as k rises from 2 to 50 images (R16, R17). Baseline from the original: one SoLU neuron that was clean on its top (pre-LayerNorm) examples was much more often unrelated at low post-LayerNorm activations (one neuron, unblinded; R7).

OpenAI vs Anthropic metrics flip the ranking of GPT2-SAE against CRATE, and the sign of CRATE-SAE's change (-10.2 under OpenAI TaR vs +34.8 under Anthropic) (r32-r34, r36). Raw top-context purity and shuffle-corrected specificity reorder MoE, dense and MoWE (reordered, not reversed): raw purity MoE 0.630 > MoWE 0.601 > dense 0.573 (r11-r13); specificity MoWE 0.523 > dense 0.375 > MoE 0.268 (r1-r3). MoE goes from first to last, while MoWE stays above dense under both scores. Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct L19 neuron 5183: Transluce's description of it scores 0.77 on simulation but has near-zero Purity (R17). MS vs AIS reverse the ordering of raw DINOv2 units against SAE features (text).

method_sensitivity.factor: Composition of the scoring sample (top-and-random vs within-fragment or corpus-wide inputs)
method_sensitivity.what: Pythia-70M residual stream layer 2: neuron-basis directions score above random under top-and-random scoring, but many show low to zero within-fragment correlation (text; the verdict cites related rows r5-r7). Pythia-70M MLP layer 1: adding bias+ReLU to the neuron basis and to random directions gave no noticeable improvement in top-and-random scores (Fig. 1; figure only). The text says random-only scores perhaps rise slightly (Fig. 3) (r4). Explainer GPT-4, simulator GPT-3.5. GPT-2 XL: GPT-4 simulation scoring on 5 top-activating and 5 random examples rated neurons ≥0.8 that show many off-explanation activations among activating inputs found over a large corpus. Among those neurons, F1 correlates −0.1 with the GPT-4 score (text).

method_sensitivity.factor: Reference dataset, conditioning variables and lexical confounds
method_sensitivity.what: Evaluation dataset: BERT-base units average 2.5 distinct patterns across QQP, QNLI, Wiki and Books (R2). Feature dataset: Pythia 70M FKR is 5.2% (Natural Language), 21.8% (Data Subset) and 67% (Code Language) at 1% inhibition (R25-R27). Conditioning set: linear-RNN neurons are single-source with all three objects conditioned on (R8) and mixed when one is omitted (R9). Word form: ≈57% of activating pairs of flagged GPT-2 neurons share a word form (r27).

method_sensitivity.factor: Clustering parameters (distance threshold, number of clusters, refinement)
method_sensitivity.what: Inception V3 neuron 1 forms two clusters at dmax 14-17 and one above 17 (r5, r6); neuron 35 has 3 vs 2 clusters (r4). PURE with two clusters misses the third semantic of ResNet-50 neurons #1177 and #141 (r12, r13). AND: the share of polysemantic neurons varies with τ and top-K across AST, BEATs-finetuned and BEATs-frozen (r4-r6). CoE: clustering removes on average 3.5 atoms per concept (r12).

method_sensitivity.factor: Embedding, similarity or attribution model used for scoring
method_sensitivity.what: ResNet-50 penultimate layer, neurons #614 and #1055: CLIP-embedding clustering and PURE attribution clustering both split into k=2 clusters but give unaligned cluster assignments, because same-class samples (lacewing, buckeye) have very small attribution distances. The text does not say either method judges these neurons mixed or pure, so the scorer changes the assignment, not the classification (r23; V7 state partial per the checker). #271: CLIP separates dogs from windmills, while attributions show one shared triangular-shape semantic (r24). PSI D-scores under two CLIP text heads correlate ρ≈0.21 (r19). The interpretability index rises with the LPIPS layer used for scoring (R7; figure only). CoE on ResNet50/101/152: the depth trend in average CPE reverses between relevance-based and activation-based patch selection (r9, r10). MMI-based concepts give lower CPE, reported for ResNet152 only (r11).

Baseline from the original: on baseline-transformer neurons, the stricter annotator found ~20% interpretable against ~40% for the other two, while SoLU neurons were ~60% for all three (R5). BERT: pattern rates per direction range from 0.56 to 1.6 across annotators (verdict reason, Table 6; no row).

In AlexNet, selectivity measures disagree in the hidden layers conv5, fc6 and fc7 (R1-R10), but human activation-maximisation interpretations and class measures agree at about 95% for fc8 output units (R16).

status_amendment.public_note: The status no longer says that no causal tests were run: two studies also used causal tests (ablation, interventions) whose summaries report results that depend on how neurons are measured, though no detailed results from these tests were extracted. It also states more clearly which study shares an author with the original paper, and the level stays R2.
